name: Crucible Industries Furnace CF-15 'Meltdown'
description:
A vehicle-mounted continuous-beam thermal weapon that projects a 30kW infrared laser capable of cutting through armored vehicles, structural steel, and reinforced concrete. The Furnace is not a precision weapon — it is a demolition tool mounted on a weapon platform.

Crucible designed the CF-15 for breaching operations where explosive charges are impractical or insufficient. The continuous beam can cut a human-sized opening in a reinforced concrete wall in under 8 seconds, and its thermal effect on personnel caught in the beam path is instantaneous and catastrophic. The weapon requires vehicle-grade power supply and cooling systems, making it unsuitable for dismounted operation.

The Meltdown has earned its nickname from several incidents where the weapon's beam was sustained longer than intended, heating structural elements to the point of failure. Two building collapses in GLMZ have been attributed to CF-15 engagements where the operator failed to account for the thermal load on load-bearing structures.
legality: Military restricted — heavy directed energy authorization
specifications:
caliber: N/A — continuous infrared beam
effective_range: 50-500 meters
rate_of_fire: Continuous beam, adjustable duration
capacity: N/A — limited by power supply
weight: 340 kg (weapon and cooling system)
power_source: Vehicle fusion reactor, draws 60kW sustained
tactical_use: The Furnace is deployed for deliberate breaching of hardened positions, destruction of armored vehicles, and denial of reinforced structures. The weapon's continuous beam allows the operator to trace cutting paths through material, effectively using the laser as a thermal saw. In anti-vehicle roles, the CF-15 can disable an armored vehicle by cutting through its engine compartment or crew cabin in a sustained 3-second exposure.
cultural_context: The Meltdown's destructive power has made it a symbol of corporate excess — a weapon so powerful it can accidentally collapse buildings. Environmental activists point to the CF-15 as evidence that corporate military technology has exceeded any reasonable definition of proportional force. Crucible's defense is that the weapon is 'precisely destructive' — it destroys only what the operator aims at. The building collapses, they argue, were operator error.
story_hooks: A CF-15 was used to cut through the wall of a bank vault during what appears to be a corporate-sponsored heist. The thermal signature was detected by satellite, and now three different intelligence agencies want to know which corporation sanctioned the operation.
Crucible has developed a miniaturized Furnace variant that can be backpack-mounted, reducing the beam power to 8kW but making it man-portable. The prototype is missing from their testing facility.

physical_description.visual_profile: A brutalist thermal projector assembly mounted on a heavy armature — blocky, industrial, purposeful. The business end is dominated by a massive cylindrical barrel shroud housing the infrared emitter, flanked by brutal heat-sink fins and cooling jacket vents. Looks less like a weapon and more like a piece of demolition equipment bolted to a tank.
physical_description.dimensions: Overall length 240cm, barrel shroud diameter 18cm, mounting footprint 80cm × 60cm, emitter lens assembly 12cm diameter
physical_description.weight_description: Crushingly heavy — 340kg of steel and composite engineering. Requires vehicle mounting; the weapon system itself has the heft of an industrial engine block. Feels immobile, permanent, designed to stay put and burn.
physical_description.primary_material: Hardened steel frame with composite heat-resistant barrel shroud (ceramic-matrix composite), aluminum cooling jacket, reinforced titanium mounting brackets
physical_description.finish: Matte industrial gray-black with visible thermal stress marks — areas around the barrel shroud show discoloration from sustained heat cycling. Cooling fins are brushed bare metal with oxidation patina in seams. Welding seams are rough, unpolished — function over aesthetics.
physical_description.color_scheme: Gunmetal gray primary with charred black heat-stress zones around the emitter. Accent colors include dull copper-red oxidation on exposed cooling surfaces and reflective danger-stripe yellow/black bands on the mounting arms.
physical_description.grip_texture: Not applicable for hand operation — weapon features vehicle-mounted control interfaces with rubberized haptic feedback grips on operator console. Physical contact points (maintenance access panels) are textured bare steel, cold and unforgiving.
distinctive_features: Massive infrared emitter lens assembly with visible thermal window (appears slightly opalescent)
Brutal aluminum cooling fins radiating from barrel shroud — some visibly warped from heat stress
Thermal bleed vents along the cooling jacket, darkened from heat exhaust
Red maintenance access panels on mounting frame with Φ cost warnings stenciled in white
Targeting laser sight mounted on upper rail (green laser point)
Heavy-gauge cable bundling for power and cooling fluid circulation
Scorch marks and melted composite residue along barrel shroud edges from previous engagements
DANGER: EXTREME THERMAL HAZARD placard in Mandarin, Spanish, and English on mounting arm
physical_description.manufacturer_markings: Crucible Industries logo (stylized furnace icon) stamped into steel frame at 45° angle. Serial plate mounted on rear cooling jacket in white-lettered black anodized aluminum. 'CF-15 MELTDOWN' designation stenciled in aggressive capitals down the left side of barrel shroud.
physical_description.condition_typical: Field-worn and heat-damaged. Operational units show blackened scorch marks, warped fins, and cooling fluid stains. Mounting hardware shows signs of repeated thermal stress. Some examples display jury-rigged reinforcement plating around the cooling jacket — evidence of catastrophic overheating incidents.
